messages:
alex: Postmortem follow-up — noticed a recurring triage gap for GPU OOM / runtime OOM incidents (3 in last 6 weeks). I think we should add an explicit 'OOM triage' section to the runtime runbook: quick checks, commands, and escalation path.

maria: +1. Can you paste the minimal command checklist you ran? would help for the PR.

alex: Sure, here's the short checklist we used during the outage: 
- Confirm impacted model shard pool and instance ids
- Capture last 200k tokens of logs and tail stderr for the runtime process
- If KV cache growth is suspected, check per-request seq lengths and cache hit rate

Commands I ran: 
```
# list pods with restarts in inference namespace
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount

# tail runtime logs for the pod (use the pod name from above)
kubectl logs -n inference POD_NAME -c runtime --since=30m | tail -n 500

# look for CUDA OOM in dmesg on node (ssh to node from bastion)
ssh node-xyz 'sudo dmesg | grep -i oom
'

# quick check for sequence length distribution via metrics API
curl -sS http://metrics.internal/api/seq-dist?model=redwood-2 | jq .
```

alex: Proposed runbook additions (short bullets): 
- Immediate triage (0-10m): run checklist above, add incident tag `oom-runtime`
- Containment (10-30m): scale down batch size by 50%, route traffic to warm fallback variant
- Escalation (30-60m): if errors persist, page eng-sre and assigned model owner, add canary fallback to model-vX-quantized
- Post-incident (within 48h): open PR to runbook with exact commands + knobs to tune

jamie: Can we standardize the commands so they're copy-paste? I volunteer to convert to a little script `oom-triage.sh` and put in ops-scripts.

maria: Action items suggestion: 
- Action: alex -> draft runbook text with the checklist and proposed escalation steps. Due: 2026-04-10 
- Action: jamie -> create `oom-triage.sh` script and example run in dev environment. Due: 2026-04-14 
- Action: oliver -> own the playbook PR review and merge, coordinate on-call training. Due: 2026-04-20

oliver: I'll take the PR review + training. Also want a short run-through in the next SRE sync so oncall knows where to find the commands.

alex: tagging @oncall here so the team sees the updated escalation path. Also flagged two recurring patterns we should document: 
1) sudden spike in max_seq_length at ~t+2h after model rollout -> often correlated with a client mis-configured batching parameter
2) GPU mem spikes tied to unsupported quantization fallback (we accidentally used a float fallback for a quantized kernel)

sre-bot: Reminder: create incident follow-up ticket and link this thread. 

jamie: For the script, I’ll include safety checks and a dry-run mode. Will add a `--escalate` flag that will ping `#eng-sre` and open the ticket template.

maria: small ask: can we add a single-line checklist at the top of the runbook (one-liner for oncall) e.g., "If OOM: run oom-triage.sh POD_NAME && scale batch -50%". That helps reduce cognitive load under page.

alex: Agreed. I'll draft that one-liner + a short explanation. Will open the runbook PR today and assign to oliver for review.

oliver: Received. I'll block 30 mins in my calendar for triage training next Wed.

maria: :white_check_mark: Thanks everyone. Once PR merged, can we add a note to the incident board and set a recurring check to see if the pattern re-occurs monthly?

alex: Yes — I'll add a follow-up card to the postmortem board and set a monthly recurrence for 3 months.

oncall: Acknowledged — will try the runbook dry-run in staging after Jamie's script is in.

sre-bot: Incident follow-up ticket created: https://tracker.internal/INC-2026-8931 (assigned to alex, jamie, oliver).
